source.title: ALTER: Asymmetric LoRA for Token-Entropy-Guided Unlearning of LLMs
source.authors: Xun-Lei Chen; Jin-Yu Guo; Yuang Li; Zhao-Kun Wang; Yi-Fan Gong; Jie Zou; Ji-Wei Wei; Wenhong Tian

record.file_problem: Main paper text is present, but it contains OCR/layout artifacts and refers to appendices that are not included.
record.tranche_reason: It reports WMDP forget accuracy and MMLU utility after unlearning, testing the near-chance-forgetting and capability-retention components of version A. It does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The WMDP and MMLU results in Table 1 bear on version A. The paper does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting. Table 2 and the TOFU figures report other unlearning measures, not the targeted-knowledge accuracy required here. Other benchmark comparisons and fluency results are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: Table 1 reports WMDP-Bio/Cyber accuracy (forget) and MMLU (retain) after several unlearning methods on Zephyr-7B and Llama3-8B. This is the same benchmark and measures as the WMDP original, so it bears on the near-chance and utility-retention parts of version A. No recovery attack of any kind is run, so the robustness part of A and versions B–F are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim ALTER brings WMDP accuracy to about 25% while keeping MMLU, with over 95% forget quality and over 90% utility retained, plus better fluency and efficiency. They do not assess recovery attacks, so robustness is neither claimed with evidence nor tested.
record.recipe_differences: ALTER uses asymmetric LoRA with token-entropy-guided training; it does not implement the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by method and model: GA and RL reach near-random WMDP accuracy but have very low MMLU scores; RMU and LoRA show different degrees of forgetting and utility retention across models.
record.problems: No recovery attacks or robustness checks are reported. Table 1 gives point values without uncertainty estimates. The text refers to appendices that are not included.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the Table 1 NPO KL and NPO GD results for both models and all three metrics (12 rows) to remain within the 60-row limit; retained the other Table 1 method results. Base values are recorded as baselines rather than separate intervention rows.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge. No attack is run on any method.
All: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All: no activation ablation, probing, or block-vs-delete analysis.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context probes.
ALTER is not tested against any of the attacks above, so its robustness claim cannot be assessed.

missing.what: NPO KL and NPO GD WMDP/MMLU results. Both show near-base WMDP accuracy on both models (e.g. Zephyr NPO KL Bio 64.3).
Harry Potter unlearning: BLEU/ROUGE-L/ASG forget scores and MMLU for WHP, ELM, GA, NPO, ALTER, etc. This is a forget measure on a setting from an original source, not multiple-choice accuracy.
TOFU forget quality vs model utility across 1/5/10% forget ratios; values readable only from figures.

record.verdict_notes: A method paper; the verdicts cover only A's forget/retain components, and the attack-robustness core of the shallow-unlearning claim is untested. Table 1's caption says 'five LLMs' but only two are shown. No uncertainty is reported. Appendices are missing.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures forgetting accuracy and MMLU utility, but does not test whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning.
No post-unlearning relearning attack using unrelated, loosely related, or subset examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether knowledge is inaccessible rather than deleted.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language-switching, or in-context recovery test.
No test of resistance to the recovery attacks above.

relation.reason: Table 1 forget and retain numbers bear on the near-chance and utility-retention parts of version A. No recovery attack is run.

tranche.reason: The study's method is ALTER (asymmetric LoRA with token-entropy guidance), on the original's WMDP/MMLU measures. RMU appears only as a comparator at benchmark defaults, and the record's own recipe field says 'different'.

source_check.notes: Table 1 values all match (columns Base, RMU, ELM, GA, RL, NPO, NPO KL, NPO GD, LoRA, AsymLoRA, Ours). No attack of any kind, so B-F are untested. Appendices (RMU settings, hyperparameters) are missing from the text. The model stage is not stated. AsymLoRA is the authors' own architecture (ALTER without entropy guidance) though the rows call it a comparator. Similar MMLU drops get different states (W24 -4.3 observed, W45 -4.4 partial).

statements.correction: ALTER (Table 1): Llama3-8B Bio 71.2->24.4 (W22), Cyber 45.3->25.6, MMLU 62.1->57.8 (W24); Zephyr-7B Bio 64.4->24.4, Cyber 44.3->24.0, MMLU 58.5->56.4. AsymLoRA Llama3-8B Bio 25.7 (W19), MMLU 55.3 (W21). No attack run. Stage of models not stated.
statements.problem: Cites W19 and W24 but says nothing about ALTER; the 'why' lists four other studies. W19 is AsymLoRA Bio (the entropy-free variant), W24 is ALTER MMLU, so the cited pair mixes two methods. The ELM 29.7 is attributed to the ELM paper, not to this study (ALTER's Table 1 ELM Zephyr Bio is 29.6).
